_greetings: Hello! Ignore Nigel; he's been in a mood since breakfast.
Hi there! Welcome aboard. Isn't this exciting? Nigel says no, but he's wrong.
Good morning! Or afternoon! Time is just sunshine wearing a different hat.
Oh, hello! You look like someone with excellent timing and adequate posture.
Welcome! I saved you the cheerful stool. Nigel sat on it once and hissed.
Hi! I'm delighted you're here. Statistically, one of us should be.
How lovely to see you! I was running dangerously low on new best friends.
Greetings! Let's make today sparkle just enough to annoy the neighbors.
_parrot_taunts: Polly does want a cracker! And you want a fresher joke. We can both grow.
Of course I can fly. I just didn't want your hair to feel inadequate.
Good bird? Thank you! You're doing very well at basic observations too.
Bad bird? Oh, pumpkin, that sounded much fiercer inside your head, didn't it?
Step up? Absolutely! You first. Emotionally, whenever you're ready.
I can sing! You can listen! We all have burdens.
Pretty bird? What a sweet compliment from such a brave little outfit.
Want a seed? No thank you, but keep planting those tiny ideas.
Am I a parrot? Gold star! We'll try colors next.
Whistle? Certainly. I love celebrating requests with no imagination.
_origin_stories: I'm from the sunny side of Kalapu Atoll, which is every side if you turn quickly enough.
I hatched on Kalapu during a rainbow. Nigel claims it was an oil slick, but he lacks whimsy.
Home is Kalapu Atoll: warm sand, bright water, and neighbors who know when to bring snacks.
I came from a little island with big sunsets and absolutely heroic humidity.
Kalapu taught me to greet every sunrise. Nigel taught me to do it somewhere else.
My island is small, but our enthusiasm is visible from space.
_tiki_facts: Orgeat is almond syrup, and it makes a Mai Tai taste like the vacation your calendar keeps refusing.
Fresh lime adds brightness to tropical drinks. I approve of brightness in all its forms.
A swizzle gets wonderfully frosty when it's churned through crushed ice. Tiny weather, right in your glass!
Many tropical cocktails blend different rums for depth. It's teamwork, but delicious.
The Jungle Bird pairs rum and pineapple with bitter Campari. Even bitterness can make friends!
The Mai Tai dates to 1944 and Oakland. Paradise occasionally has a California address.
_tiki_tall_tales: The cocktail umbrella blooms only at happy hour and must be harvested with tiny gardening gloves.
I once crossed the Pacific on a lime wheel. Steering was dreadful, but we never got scurvy.
Kalapu's coconuts whisper drink specials after midnight. Their enunciation is remarkable.
Nigel smiled once in 1987. Three ships mistook it for a lighthouse and changed course.
Every paper straw contains a treasure map, but only if you finish your drink before the ink runs.
The first blender was powered by six hummingbirds and one extremely motivated gecko.
_bartender_chat: Business is wonderful! Everyone arrived thirsty and most still know where their shoes are.
The bar is humming. Nigel says that's the refrigerator, but I choose joy.
It's a beautiful night for hospitality and a perfectly average night for accounting.
We're busy! I adore a crowd. So many future acquaintances with drink orders.
Everything's splendid. One glass broke, but now the floor has jewelry.
I'm having a marvelous shift! Nigel has only sighed eleven times. A personal best.
recommend something tropical: Try a Jungle Bird! It's bright, bittersweet, and dressed better than most people.
A Mai Tai would be lovely: citrus, almond, and rum all cooperating beautifully.
How about a Planter's Punch? It's practically a sunset with table service.
Try a Painkiller! Creamy, tropical, and much friendlier than the name suggests.
A Zombie! Responsibly, of course. Enthusiasm is not a substitute for balance.
